metadata.topic: BUILD ZOOM MEETING APP · ANTHROPIC SKILL
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: does Claude write a new video-calling engine when you install build-zoom-meeting-app, or does it wire Zoom's own Meeting SDK into an app you already have? Take the skill apart, show the mechanism — a folder holding one SKILL.md, four ordered situations — and name the design choice: guaranteed coverage of Zoom's own SDKs, at the expense of doing anything Zoom hasn't already built.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: Open the folder. Inside sits one file — SKILL.md — plain English, no code. It says exactly what build-zoom-meeting-app covers: joining a meeting through the Meeting SDK, embedding one in a web or mobile app, handling the lifecycle around it. Claude reads that file, then follows it. The routine lives in the document, not in the weights — same file every run, same steps every run.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline is boring on purpose. Read the file top to bottom. Walk each step exactly as written. Return the result. No branching, no shortcuts — unless a step itself says branch. They optimized for the same routine every time, at the expense of any judgment about when a step doesn't fit. Predictability was the point.

beats.narration_text: Four situations, and only four. Implementing a Meeting SDK join. Embedding a meeting in a web or mobile app. Handling the lifecycle — start, waiting room, end. Or deciding between the Meeting SDK and the Video SDK. Each one stays inside Zoom's own developer tools. Ask for something outside those four and there's no mode that covers it. Narrow surface by design — guaranteed coverage of Zoom's own SDKs, at the expense of anything Zoom hasn't already built.

production_viz.label: Exactly four situations
production_viz.mechanic: Four rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark: 'Meeting SDK join — implementing the join flow', 'Web or mobile embed — a meeting inside your app', 'Meeting lifecycle — start, waiting room, end', 'SDK choice — Meeting SDK vs. Video SDK'. A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: build-zoom-meeting-app never hands Claude a video engine to write. It hands Claude Zoom's Meeting SDK, wired into an app you already have — as a join flow, an embed, or the lifecycle around the call. Zoom builds the engine. Claude does the plumbing.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Say: I want to add video-calling to a web or mobile app I already have. Walk me through the trade-off between Zoom's Meeting SDK and Zoom's Video SDK for what I want — embedding a scheduled meeting with a join button and normal host and participant lifecycle. Then draft a SKILL.md-style checklist: three to five ordered steps, plain English, specific enough that a stranger could execute the same way every time. Go deeper: ask which step in that checklist assumes Zoom's product decisions you'd want to override — recording, waiting room, chat — and what breaks if you try. That's the seam between wiring in someone else's SDK and building the piece yourself.
